claims.text: The baseline alloy has the nominal composition NbTaHfTiZr.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZr alloy is a fully disordered BCC solid solution.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZr alloy has good room-temperature ductility.
The intervention is addition of vanadium at a nominal coefficient of 0.5 to produce NbTaHfTiZrV0.5.
The proposed vanadium addition is approximately 0.5 mole fraction.
Vanadium atoms will integrate into the BCC matrix without causing deleterious phase separation.
Adding vanadium will enhance lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5.
Vanadium-induced lattice distortion will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion will increase the alloy's high-temperature yield strength.
Vanadium's relatively low atomic weight helps limit the density of the modified alloy.
The proposed vanadium concentration will not cause a significant increase in overall alloy density.
The controlled vanadium concentration will preserve room-temperature plasticity.
At temperatures of at least 800 °C under compression or tension, NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 will have approximately 20–30% higher yield strength than NbTaHfTiZr.
NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 will maintain room-temperature ductility comparable to that of NbTaHfTiZr.
Refractory HEAs can exhibit strong mechanical capability above 800 °C.
The intervention is expected to be effective primarily in solid-solution BCC refractory HEAs.
Vanadium additions above the optimized concentration may cause phase instability or degraded ductility.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy shows less than a 20% high-temperature yield-strength increase or more than a 10% reduction in room-temperature ductility relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The phrase '0.5 mole fraction' normally denotes 50 at.% V, whereas NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 denotes a V stoichiometric coefficient of 0.5 and approximately 9.09 at.% V after normalization. These are materially different concentrations unless 'mole fraction' was intended to mean stoichiometric coefficient.
